sources.entry: Postgres.app - The easiest way to get started with PostgreSQL on the Mac.

summary.one_liner: Postgres.app is a macOS app that runs PostgreSQL servers from a menu bar GUI, bundling PostgreSQL with common extensions and command line tools.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a native Mac app with a GUI to start and stop PostgreSQL servers and lets you run multiple PostgreSQL versions at once. On first launch it initialises a database cluster, starts the server, and creates a superuser and a database named after your user. The app bundles PostgreSQL along with PostGIS, pgrouting, wal2json, pldebugger, pgvector, plv8 or pljs depending on version, and a set of CLI tools such as psql, pg_dump, pgbench, and GDAL/PROJ utilities. The README also describes how to build the PostgreSQL binaries and the Swift GUI from source using makefiles in the src-xx directories. It documents enabling the pl/pgsql debugger via shared_preload_libraries and the pldbgapi extension.
use_cases: run PostgreSQL locally on a Mac
test multiple PostgreSQL versions side by side
develop spatial queries with PostGIS on macOS
try pgvector for embeddings on a Mac
build PostgreSQL binaries from source for macOS
how_to_run: Download Postgres.app from the Postgres.app website or the GitHub releases page
Move the app to your Applications folder and open it
Start a server from the menu bar GUI
Use the bundled psql or other CLI tools from /Applications/Postgres.app/Contents/Versions
To build binaries: run make in a src-xx directory (see README prerequisites)
notable: Runs the server as your own user rather than a separate postgres system user
Multiple PostgreSQL major versions can run simultaneously
Bundles PostGIS, pgvector, pgrouting and other extensions
Binaries and GUI are built separately, with version-specific macOS and Xcode build environments documented
caveats: macOS only; the GUI is a native Mac app
Building the binaries from source downloads many gigabytes and needs MacPorts or Homebrew prerequisites; PostGIS and plv8 take a long time
Some extensions depend on PostgreSQL version (plv8 up to 13, pgvector and pgrouting from 15)
